newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL BE ANTI-INFLATIONARY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL BE ANTI-INFLATIONARY.

text.p: Greece's 1997 forex policy will remain focused on fighting inflation and the drachma will be stable but more flexible versus currencies making up the ecu, a high-level central bank official told Reuters.

"The main goal of the foreign exchange policy is to combat inflation," said the high-level Bank of Greece official. "As the governor stated on Friday, the drachma will be stable but more flexible versus the main currencies that make up the ecu."
The central bank official said the magnitude of trade flows between Greece and other EU countries defined the main currencies that make up the ecu.

Asked if the central bank had formed and targeted a trade-weighted foreign exchange index containing the currencies that make up the ecu, he said that no such index was mentioned in the governor's policy speech last Friday. Therefore no such index was being followed.

A Sunday press report said that the central bank would be targeting a basket of currencies that make up the ecu but using different weights defined by the magnitude of trade flows between Greece and other EU countries.
"We, at the central bank, place great importance on credibility and we intend to preserve it," said the official.
